surface_note: Catalogued from the Python agent tool registry, not from `prism tools`. `prism tools` merges this registry with the Rust command-tools (crates/agent/src/command_tools.rs) and any MCP servers found at runtime; those Rust tools are thin wrappers over `prism <subcommand>` and cannot exist without the PRISM binary, so they are not separately installable and have nothing to publish. Only the Python registry holds tools with their own pip dependencies. The registry is 92 tools by default and 89 with PRISM_DISABLE_MEMORY=1 (the three artifact-store tools register only when the memory subsystem is on); every one of the 92 is judged here.

entries.name: PRISM
entries.description: PRISM itself — the agentic materials-discovery workspace: a terminal UI and CLI that plans and runs materials campaigns, calls the tools listed elsewhere in this catalog, records every call in a local provenance ledger, and connects to the platform for compute, knowledge and billing. Installs as a single self-contained binary (macOS arm64, Linux x86_64/aarch64, Windows x86_64) plus a Python tool layer. Read `known_issues` before downloading: the currently published release is v1.0.0 from 2026-07-03 and has real platform limits.
entries.author: Mirdyne

install.note: install.sh resolves the latest GitHub release for your uname -s/-m and unpacks the matching archive. Check `platforms` and `known_issues` first — on an unsupported platform the installer will fetch an archive that does not run.

alternatives.note: Python tool layer only — no TUI binary.
The only path that gets you current code; the published release is stale (see known_issues).

platforms.verified_from: GitHub release v1.0.0 asset list, read 2026-07-27
missing: prism-macos-x86_64.tar.gz — the release workflow declares a macos-15-intel matrix leg but no such asset exists in v1.0.0, so Intel Macs have no binary and install.sh will 404 for them

known_issues: STALE RELEASE: the only published release is v1.0.0 (2026-07-03). Development has continued well past it; anything installed from that tag is months behind.

RETIRED BACKEND: v1.0.0's `prism query` still defaults --neo4j-url to http://localhost:7474 and --qdrant-url to http://localhost:6333. Neo4j and Qdrant were dropped in favour of Turso, so that path in the shipped binary points at services PRISM no longer runs.

LINUX GLIBC FLOOR: the Linux archives are built on GitHub's ubuntu-latest / ubuntu-24.04-arm runners (glibc 2.39), so they do not run on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35) or older. Build from source on those systems.

verification.note: The published artifacts were NOT downloaded or executed for this entry. What was verified: the v1.0.0 release exists with the five assets listed under `platforms.available` (GitHub API); the release build matrix in .github/workflows/native-release.yml at tag v1.0.0 uses ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04-arm for the Linux legs, which is the basis for the glibc claim; and `git show v1.0.0:crates/cli/src/main.rs` still carries the Neo4j/Qdrant defaults. This entry is published with those constraints stated rather than gated, so the hub is not empty — but it must be replaced by a fresh release entry once one is cut.

entries.name: PRISM MCP Server
entries.description: PRISM's whole materials tool layer exposed over the Model Context Protocol on stdio, so any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, an SDK agent) can call the same search, prediction, CALPHAD, simulation and dataset tools the PRISM TUI calls. Each tool keeps its own dependency gate: a tool whose extra is absent returns an install hint rather than failing the session.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.note: Ships inside PRISM; run `python3 -m app.mcp_server` from a PRISM checkout or venv and point your MCP client's stdio transport at it. prism-platform is NOT on PyPI as of 2026-07-27 — use the wheel from the GitHub release or a source checkout.

verification.note: scripts/smoke-mcp-direct.py --server python --filter materials_search drove `python3 -m app.mcp_server` over JSON-RPC stdio: the server advertised 51 tools and materials_search returned a 383 KB real payload in 9.52 s (PASS 1 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 0).

entries.name: PRISM Materials Search
entries.description: Federated structure and property search across public materials databases. `materials_search` fans out over the keyless OPTIMADE federation (COD, Alexandria, OQMD, ...) and normalises hits to one schema with per-source attribution; `query_materials_project` queries Materials Project directly via MP_API_KEY or, when logged in, the platform proxy. No extra required — both dependencies ship in a default PRISM install.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.note: Ships with every PRISM install; no additional extra needed.

verification.note: materials_search(query='TiO2', limit=2) returned a real COD structure (id 1000000, C5H17AlN2O8P2) with lattice vectors and source attribution; two OPTIMADE providers (alexandria pbe/pbesol) returned HTTP 500 and were reported per-source rather than hidden. query_materials_project(formula='TiO2') returned MP entries with band_gap/formation_energy via the MARC27 platform proxy after the local MP_API_KEY path reported it was unset.

entries.name: PRISM Property Prediction
entries.description: Composition-to-property machine learning for materials. `model_train` pulls training rows from Materials Project (or a local dataset), featurises formulas with matminer Magpie descriptors and fits a scikit-learn / XGBoost / LightGBM regressor; `predict` applies a trained model to a new formula, or runs a pre-trained matgl GNN on a crystal structure. Every prediction carries a provenance block naming the feature backend and model. Requires the `[ml]` extra.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.command: pip install scikit-learn xgboost lightgbm optuna pymatgen matminer matgl matplotlib pyarrow joblib robocrystallographer
install.note: prism-platform is NOT on PyPI (verified 2026-07-27, HTTP 404), so `command` names the distributions directly — that always works inside an existing PRISM venv. `extra_command` resolves only from a source checkout or the wheel attached to the GitHub release. Without these, `predict` and `model_train` return {"error", "install_hint", "requires_extra"} instead of an ImportError; `list_models` and `list_predictable_properties` work on a default install.

dependency_licenses.matminer: BSD-3-Clause (LBNL modified BSD, from the LICENSE shipped in matminer 0.10.1)

verification.note: model_train(property_name='band_gap', algorithm='random_forest', max_samples=200) trained on 200 real Materials Project rows with 134 matminer/0.10.1 Magpie features (MAE 0.709 eV, R2 -0.036 at that sample size — the tool reports the metrics, it does not claim they are good) and wrote ~/.prism/ml_models/band_gap_random_forest.joblib. predict(target='formula', formula='LiCoO2') then returned 1.635 eV with a full provenance block. predict(target='structure', ...) reported the honest matgl install hint because matgl is absent here. predict_properties was exercised only on a 3-row dataset and correctly refused with 'insufficient data or features'.

entries.name: PRISM CALPHAD Thermodynamics
entries.description: CALPHAD phase equilibria on TDB thermodynamic databases. `calphad` manages the TDB store in ~/.prism/databases and lists phases; `calphad_compute` runs equilibrium, phase-diagram and Gibbs-energy calculations through pycalphad; `analyze_phases` chains load-phases-equilibrium into one phase-stability summary. Every number comes out of pycalphad — PRISM parses no thermodynamics of its own and converts no units. Requires the `[calphad]` extra.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.note: prism-platform is NOT on PyPI (verified 2026-07-27, HTTP 404) — `command` is the form that works inside an existing PRISM venv. pycalphad caps at Python 3.14; on a newer interpreter PRISM proxies these tools into an auto-provisioned Python 3.12 science sidecar (~/.prism/venv-sci). User data (TDB files) lives in ~/.prism/databases and is not supplied by this entry.

verification.note: pycalphad is NOT installed on the verification host, so the equilibrium path was not executed. What was verified: calphad(action='list_databases') returns {'databases': [], 'count': 0} without pycalphad; calphad(action='list_phases', ...), calphad_compute(action='equilibrium', ...) and analyze_phases all return the honest {error, install_hint: "pip install 'prism-platform[calphad]'", requires_extra: 'calphad'} dict rather than raising ImportError. Numerical correctness of the calculations is asserted by the pycalphad-verified constants documented in app/tools/simulation/calphad_bridge.py, not by this catalogue.

entries.name: PRISM Atomistic Simulation
entries.description: pyiron-backed atomistic simulation control plane: build and inspect structures (`structure`), submit and poll relaxation / MD jobs (`sim_run`, `sim_job`), enumerate available interatomic potentials (`list_potentials`), run k-point and cutoff convergence sweeps (`run_convergence_test`), read the HPC queue (`check_hpc_queue`) and execute multi-step pyiron workflows (`run_workflow`). Requires the `[simulation]` extra.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.note: prism-platform is NOT on PyPI (verified 2026-07-27, HTTP 404) — `command` is the form that works inside an existing PRISM venv. pyiron caps at Python 3.14; on a newer interpreter PRISM proxies these tools into an auto-provisioned Python 3.12 science sidecar (~/.prism/venv-sci), which pins pyiron_atomistics>=0.5,<0.6 rather than the >=0.6 the extra declares.

verification.note: pyiron_atomistics is NOT installed on the verification host and the science sidecar was NOT provisioned, so no simulation was executed end-to-end. What was verified: sim_run and list_potentials return the honest {error, install_hint: "pip install 'prism-platform[simulation]'", requires_extra: 'simulation'} dict rather than raising. Do not read this entry as a claim that pyiron runs on this build — PRISM's own tool catalogue records the pyiron install as blocked on an HDF5 build failure.

entries.name: PRISM Dataset Workbench
entries.description: The tabular half of a materials campaign: import/export and validate datasets (`dataset`), filter and rank candidates against numeric criteria (`select_materials`), plot property distributions and correlation matrices (`plot`), write a markdown campaign report (`generate_report`) and turn a candidate table into a per-material simulation job plan (`plan_simulations`). Refuses silently-wrong answers — an unmatched filter column or an unsortable rank key is an error, not a quietly unranked list. No extra required.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.note: pandas and matplotlib are default dependencies. PDF report output additionally needs the `[reports]` extra (markdown, weasyprint); without it generate_report writes Markdown and says so in `pdf_skipped` + `install_hint`.

verification.note: Ran as a chain on a 3-row CSV: dataset(action='import') -> 3 rows/3 columns; dataset(action='validate') -> completeness 1.0, no findings; select_materials(criteria={'band_gap_min': 2.5}, sort_by='band_gap', top_n=2) -> 2 of 3 selected, ranked=true; plot(kind='correlation_matrix') -> wrote catdemo_correlation.png with a real -0.9589 band_gap/density correlation; generate_report -> wrote output/catdemo_report.md; plan_simulations -> 3 planned jobs. plot() called without `kind` returns the valid-kind list rather than raising.

entries.name: PRISM Structure Import
entries.description: Bridges 'found a structure in Materials Project or a paper' to 'run a simulation on it': parses CIF text or a lattice/species/coords dict via ASE and lands it in both the MACE structure cache (returning a cache_ref) and, when pyiron is present, the pyiron StructureStore (returning a structure_id). Requires ASE, which PRISM ships in the `[mace]` extra.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.command: pip install mace-torch torch ase numpy huggingface-hub phonopy
install.note: prism-platform is NOT on PyPI (verified 2026-07-27, HTTP 404) — `command` is the form that works inside an existing PRISM venv. structure_import itself only needs ASE (`pip install ase`); the full `[mace]` set above is what the MACE primitives need, including huggingface-hub and phonopy, which were undeclared until 2026-07-27.

optional.unlocks: also lands the structure in the pyiron StructureStore and returns a structure_id; without it the result carries a pyiron_note saying so and still returns a cache_ref

license_notes: ASE is LGPL-2.1-or-later — weak copyleft. It is imported, not vendored, and PRISM's own tool code stays MIT; redistributors bundling ASE must honour the LGPL.

The `[mace]` extra installs mace-torch (MIT code). The MACE-MH-1 *weights* are licensed ASL and are NON-COMMERCIAL — see the separate `mace-mh-1` model entry in this marketplace. structure_import itself loads no weights.

verification.note: ASE is NOT installed on the verification host, so no CIF was parsed. What was verified: structure_import returns {error: 'structure_import needs ase (Atomic Simulation Environment)', install_hint: "pip install 'prism-platform[mace]'", requires_extra: 'mace'} rather than raising ImportError.

entries.name: PRISM MACE Atomistic Compute
entries.description: Atomistic compute on MACE foundation interatomic potentials: build a supercell from composition + phase and relax it to a local minimum (mace_relax_structure), equilibrate it with NVT molecular dynamics (mace_md_equilibrate), screen dynamic stability with finite-displacement harmonic phonons (mace_phonon_harmonic), and compute elastic constants (mace_compute_elastic) and dilute-solute energetics (mace_compute_dilute_solute). Every primitive is approval-gated, returns a JobHandle to poll with the bundled mace job tools, and caches results by canonical (structure, head, calc params) so re-asking is free. Feed it structures from the prism-structure-io entry — a cache_ref threads straight in. Requires the [mace] extra.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.command: pip install mace-torch torch ase numpy huggingface-hub phonopy
install.note: prism-platform is NOT on PyPI (verified 2026-07-27, HTTP 404) — `command` is the form that works inside an existing PRISM venv. Foundation weights (MACE-MP-0, MIT) are fetched on first use via huggingface-hub; ASL-licensed weights stay behind the MACE_ACCEPT_ASL_LICENSE gate.

license_notes: The [mace] extra installs mace-torch (MIT code). Verification here ran on the MIT-licensed MACE-MP-0 foundation weights from the local HuggingFace cache; ASL-licensed weights (e.g. MACE-MH-1) remain behind the MACE_ACCEPT_ASL_LICENSE gate and were not touched.
ASE is LGPL-2.1-or-later — weak copyleft. It is imported, not vendored; redistributors bundling ASE must honour the LGPL.

verification.note: Exercised end-to-end offline on 2026-08-05 (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, MACE-MP-0 weights already in the local HuggingFace cache, no network). mace_relax_structure(Fe100, bcc, backend=local) succeeded in ~1.5 s: energy_per_atom -8.3055 eV, fmax 4e-15 eV/A, cache:// structure + provenance refs. mace_md_equilibrate(T_K=300, ps=0.1) consumed that cache_ref and succeeded in 109 s: mean_T_K 214 K with RDF and trajectory refs. mace_get_job polled both jobs through the local SQLite job store to succeeded, and mace_estimate_cost(relax_structure, n_atoms=64) returned a real read-only estimate (240 s, USD 0.12). phonon_harmonic / compute_elastic / compute_dilute_solute were NOT run here; they share the supercell-build, job-store and cache paths the two runs exercised. Probing also surfaced drift between the tools' declared input schemas and their enforced validation (n_atoms declared min 8 / enforced 100, fmax declared max 1.0 / enforced 0.5, max_steps declared min 1 / enforced 10) — reported, not fixed by this catalog.

entries.name: PRISM Quantum ESPRESSO I/O
entries.description: The pyiron-free Quantum ESPRESSO path: qe_write_input builds a pw.x .in file (namelists, cutoffs, Monkhorst-Pack k-points, pseudo_dir) from any structure pymatgen can read; qe_resolve_pseudopotentials maps elements to the .upf files present in a directory; qe_parse_output turns a pw.x .out file into converged energy/forces/stress/wall time — and refuses unconverged or truncated output rather than reporting plausible-looking numbers. These tools never execute pw.x: they generate the input a real allocation consumes and read the output it produces. Requires the [qe] extra.
entries.author: Mirdyne (PRISM)

install.note: prism-platform is NOT on PyPI (verified 2026-07-27, HTTP 404) — `command` is the form that works inside an existing PRISM venv. The pw.x binary itself is not part of this entry and is not required by it: the tools generate input for, and parse output of, a pw.x run performed on whatever allocation the user has.

license_notes: ASE is LGPL-2.1-or-later — weak copyleft. It is imported, not vendored; redistributors bundling ASE must honour the LGPL.

verification.note: All three tools exercised end-to-end offline on 2026-08-05. qe_write_input wrote a real Si scf input (2-atom diamond cell, ecutwfc 60 Ry / ecutrho 480 Ry, 8x8x8 Monkhorst-Pack grid, pseudo_dir wired). qe_resolve_pseudopotentials mapped [Si] to Si.pbesol-n-rrkjus_psl.1.0.0.UPF in a local directory. qe_parse_output parsed the converged pw.x fixture shipped in tests/test_qe_io.py: converged=true, total_energy -308.6031 eV (-22.68191071 Ry via ASE units), wall time 12.0 s; the same suite asserts unconverged and truncated outputs yield explicit failures with no numbers. No pw.x binary exists on this machine and none was needed — the tools generate and parse, they do not execute.
